def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    bg=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    objects=comps(grid,4,bg)
    def area(p):
        r0,r1,c0,c1=bbox(p); return (r1-r0+1)*(c1-c0+1)
    # The boundary marker spans two sides; if absent, use the largest edge object.
    candidates=[(col,p) for col,p in objects if edge_sides(p,h,w)]
    corners=[cp for cp in candidates if len(edge_sides(cp[1],h,w))>=2]
    pool=corners if corners else candidates
    if not pool: return [row[:] for row in grid]
    keycol,key=max(pool,key=lambda cp:(area(cp[1]),len(cp[1])))
    kc=(sum(r for r,c in key)/len(key),sum(c for r,c in key)/len(key))
    def dist(p): return math.hypot(sum(r for r,c in p)/len(p)-kc[0],sum(c for r,c in p)/len(p)-kc[1])
    groups={}
    for col,p in objects: groups.setdefault(canon(p),[]).append((col,p))
    duplicate=[arr for arr in groups.values() if len(arr)>=2]
    if not duplicate: return [row[:] for row in grid]
    # Pick the repeated shape with an instance closest to the boundary marker.
    arr=min(duplicate,key=lambda arr:(min(dist(p) for col,p in arr),-len(canon(arr[0][1]))))
    target_col,target=max(arr,key=lambda cp:dist(cp[1]))
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    for r,c in target: out[r][c]=keycol
